title: script/script.json
description: The one hand-edited script file: acts of shots (or lines) with id, vo, on_screen, picture, sources, claims and notes. `slate script build` gates it and writes script/storyboard.json and script/SCRIPT.md. Unknown keys are allowed and carried through.

version.description: the change note for this draft

ids.description: renumber: the written ids are draft ids; shots are numbered <id_prefix>01… in order and mentions are remapped

timing.description: Overrides for placement and pace (seconds, words a second).

rules.description: This film's own script rules, on top of the gates every film gets.

derived_from.description: a derived film's parent script (slate variant writes it): {film, path, sha256}

cut.description: a cut-down: {target_s, keep: [the parent's shot ids to keep]}; with no acts of its own the script is those shots

translate.description: a translation: {from, to}; every shot keeps its parent's id

acts.description: Empty in a new film until someone writes the first act (`slate new` scaffolds it that way); `slate script build` refuses to build a script with no acts.

transition.description: How the shot hands to the next, in the motion law's kinds: carry, portal, mask, whip (motion-masked), ui_cut (a UI state cut with the camera locked), music_cut (a cut on a musical hit) or seam (a blend of 4 frames or less inside one generated shot). Words that name one, as the films wrote them ("Carry: the line keeps drawing", sorted into the kinds by slate.qa.checks.picture.transition_kind), or {kind, note}. Carried through storyboard.json into timing/shots.json (transition_out); `slate qa cuts` judges every scene change against it.

engine.description: the engine that draws this shot when it isn't its act's (P074; docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §8): carried through storyboard.json into timing/shots.json, where `slate render` and `slate check` read it

generate.description: a generation request for this shot (`slate gen` reads it); carried through storyboard.json into timing/shots.json

reading.description: how the shot's text is read, with its reason: {"voice_matched": true | [statements], "not_for_reading": true | [statements], "labels": true, "reason": "…"}. A voice-matched definition may pass the word budget and needs only the 1.5 s floor; a surface not for reading isn't timed; labels (the words name what the picture shows: a product's UI, a Simulator label, an end card) may pass 40% of the voice but still count toward the cap and are timed in full. Carried into storyboard.json; the script gates and `slate qa readtime` honour it, with one meaning.

oneOf.description: <source id> or <source id>:<where>, or a note

quote.description: the source's exact words this shot shows (product copy); the script's quote gate finds them at `where`

where.description: where the quote is, as path:line or path:first-last (else the part of ref after its colon)

oneOf.description: an approved claim's id or text, or a claim id in brief/truth.json
